notice: All organizations, inputs, activity and results are synthetic. This proposed workflow is not a connected employer system or measured company performance.
title: Reuse the pattern. Keep the operating context.
intro: A proposed portfolio-delivery workbench for ASG: scope repeatable GTM systems across software companies while preserving each company’s data, sales motion and operating owner.
queueIntro: All operating companies and engagements are fictional. No ASG portfolio customer records, cross-company data access or production system details are used.
workbenchIntro: Review the reusable pattern and local exceptions before a proposed deployment. This demo does not connect to Clay or share data between companies.
firstBody: Define the common field contract, adapt the segment and lifecycle rules, and pair each proposed build with an OpCo owner and a measurable outcome.

fields.label: Operating company and data boundary identified
Shared fields and local exceptions documented
Enrichment order and credit budget agreed
Bowtie stage and outcome measure agreed
Local owner and reusable documentation assigned

rules.title: Resolve the operating-company context
rules.next: Keep each company’s account records and permissions distinct before reusing a workflow.

rules.title: Adapt the play to the sales motion
rules.next: An SMB workflow and an enterprise evaluation have different qualification, timing and buyer needs.

rules.title: Define the reusable data contract
rules.next: Reuse the stable schema while documenting local field mappings and exceptions. Do not force inconsistent lifecycle definitions together.

rules.title: Set the enrichment decision rules
rules.next: Reuse known fields first, then apply a bounded provider sequence with source provenance and a budget.

rules.title: Connect the build to a lifecycle outcome
rules.next: Choose whether the work supports acquisition, activation, retention or expansion and define the denominator.

rules.title: Prepare the operating handover
rules.next: The OpCo needs an owner, failure recovery and a documented pattern that another company can adapt.

ready.title: Ready for an OpCo delivery review
ready.next: The local RevOps owner can review the schema, enrichment policy, outcome definition and handover before a scoped pilot.

experiments.name: Reusable contract with local mapping
experiments.hypothesis: A common pattern reduces reinvention without erasing business differences.
experiments.primary: Accepted deployments with a named operating owner
experiments.guardrail: Cross-company data mixing and hidden exceptions
experiments.allocation: Use matched account cohorts and a fixed observation window. Review uncertainty and selection effects before expansion.

experiments.name: Outcome-linked delivery
experiments.hypothesis: A lifecycle measure makes the value of a build inspectable.
experiments.treatment: Bowtie stage and qualified outcome measure
experiments.primary: Useful outcomes for the agreed cohort
experiments.guardrail: Activity metrics presented as revenue impact
experiments.allocation: Use matched account cohorts and a fixed observation window. Review uncertainty and selection effects before expansion.

roadmap.title: Scope with the OpCo operator
roadmap.body: Agree on the sales motion, current systems, lifecycle definitions and one high-value bottleneck.
roadmap.measure: Clear boundary, owner and success measure

roadmap.title: Pilot a documented shared pattern
roadmap.body: Build enrichment and handoff proposals with bounded costs, local mappings and visible exceptions.

roadmap.title: Contribute the proven pattern to the library
roadmap.body: Evaluate the pilot, document tradeoffs and make the next deployment easier without copying private data.
roadmap.measure: Reusable components, local adoption and lifecycle impact
